source_lines.39: Fix integers $M,q\ge1$, set $[M]=\{1,\ldots,M\}$, and write the image space on a fixed patch grid as $\mathcal X=(\mathbb R^q)^M$. A measurable space is a set with a specified sigma-algebra; equip $\mathcal X$ and a finite-dimensional latent space $\mathcal Z$ with such structures. An image is $x=(x_1,\ldots,x_M)\in\mathcal X$, with $q$ real pixel values in each of its $M$ patches. Let $S=(x^{(1)},\ldots,x^{(n)})$ be a finite training set with $n\ge1$. For $u\in\mathbb R^q$, set $\|u\|_2^2=\sum_{r=1}^q u_r^2$. For $V\subseteq[M]$ let $\mathcal Z^V=\{(z_j)_{j\in V}:z_j\in\mathcal Z\}$. For unmasked reconstruction, the encoder and decoder are deterministic measurable maps $E_\phi:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Z$ and $D_\psi:\mathcal Z\to\mathcal X$. For masked reconstruction, the encoder is a measurable deterministic map $(V,(x_j)_{j\in V})\mapsto(z_j)_{j\in V}\in\mathcal Z^V$, and the decoder maps the ordered length-$M$ sequence of encoded visible tokens and mask tokens to an element of $\mathcal X$. Each mask token is one learned vector $m\in\mathcal Z$ reused at every masked position. All maps take finite real values; when implemented by feedforward neural networks, each is a finite computation graph evaluated in the layered order of its vertices.
source_lines.53: For masked autoencoding, fix an integer $k$ with $1\le k<M$ and let $\mathcal V_k=\{V\subseteq[M]:|V|=k\}$, a set with cardinality $\binom{M}{k}$. A mask $V$ is sampled uniformly from $\mathcal V_k$; the patches in $V$ are visible and the patches in $[M]\setminus V$ are masked. The encoder receives only the visible patches, with their positions, and no mask tokens. The decoder receives the encoded visible patches and a shared learned mask token at each missing position, with position information for all $M$ slots, and outputs predictions $\hat x_j(\phi,\psi;x,V)\in\mathbb R^q$ for every patch position.
